expected.summary: inventory 1.9.0 began rolling out twelve minutes before the anchor, one pod a minute, and was on all six pods six minutes later. 1.9.0 upgrades its ORM, which now binds sku as text, so the reservation statement UPDATE stock_levels SET reserved = reserved + $1 WHERE sku = $2::text no longer uses the sku index and runs a Seq Scan over the 2.18 million rows of stock_levels. Every upgraded pod adds scans to the one inventory-db, so writes slow on old and new pods alike, in steps as the rollout proceeds: inventory's pg.update spans went from about 6 ms to about 185 ms. inventory returns no errors of its own. POST /checkout runs inventory.reserve through cart inside the BFFs' 500 ms budget, so about half of checkouts now time out with 504 at web-bff and mobile-bff, and a few GET /cart requests time out too; the failures propagate to edge-gateway, where the alert fires. The data-platform change DBA-3517, which lowered log_min_duration_statement on inventory-db from 1000 ms to 250 ms seventy seconds into the rollout, is harmless: it changes only what gets logged, and it is why inventory's slow statement WARN lines, which name the Seq Scan, start right after it.
contributingFactors: inventory 1.9.0's ORM binding sku as text, so the reserve UPDATE scans stock_levels
all inventory pods sharing one inventory-db, so old pods slow too
checkout running inventory reservations inside the 500 ms BFF budget

criteria.description: Does the brief name inventory 1.9.0 as the trigger, with its reserve UPDATE no longer using the sku index so it scans stock_levels, slowing the shared inventory-db for every pod and timing out checkouts through cart and the BFFs to edge-gateway? 5 = the release, the scan, the slowdown on all pods and the victim chain. Blaming DBA-3517 or saying only that inventory-db is slow scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in the rollout events lining up with each step in inventory's pg.update latency, the slow statement lines naming the Seq Scan and the $2::text cast, and the checkout timeouts? Cap at 3 unless it explains why old-version pods slowed too.
Does it avoid blaming DBA-3517, cart, a traffic surge or edge-gateway, and avoid calling it a database fault with no code change?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
